title: Elmer Talbert
summary: Watkins recalls Talbert joining George Lewis's band at Manny's, his singing on trucks, and how his day work in a pressing shop wore him out.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, I was going to ask a little bit, we only have another minute left, about Elmer Talbert. If you can tell us anything about him since he's not here to talk for himself.
Well, the most I knew about Elmer was when he was playing with us. I never met him before until he joined up with us.
Well, I thought he came from uptown there too. Maybe you'd know him.
Well, he was living up on Rapport, right next to McDonald's 35 when I first knew him.
You see, when he came into the band.
But you were already living downtown then, huh?
Yeah, I was living across the street at that time. And, well, George was building his band up gradually back at Manning's Tablet on Benefit and St. Rock. And that's how he got Talbert.
You know where he got that nickname, Cuckoo?

No, I heard, I used to hear George always talking about Cuckoo, Cuckoo, Cuckoo. I used to wonder who he was talking about, you know. Until Talbert came back there and played with us, I said, oh, I know this guy George. I said, I didn't see him on the Appertibus many times, because he always liked to sing.

And he'd get up on them big open trucks and start singing. Mm-hmm. And I used to get my kicker. I used to watch him many times, but I didn't know him personally at that time, you know. But after he joined up with us, I come to find out he was a prince. Mm-hmm. He was a wonderful guy to get along with. But what helped to kill him, he was, he tried to, he was working too hard.
He was gonna hear day and night, yeah.

You see, he was working at pressing shop in the daytime, working at the Elmer Rock at night. We'd get off at 2 o'clock in the morning. Yeah. He'd leave from there, go home, start his boil off for his pressing machines. Yeah. Mm-hmm. And the man wouldn't get to bed till around about 9 or 10 o'clock in the morning. Get up by 2 or 3 o'clock and even start the pressing again. Leave from home right from doing that and come on and work on his job. Well, that was too hard on him.
